title: Safe Output and Contextual Escaping
keywords: why input sanitization is not a replacement for output encoding
subtopics: Why input sanitization is not a replacement for output encoding.
learning_outcomes: Explain what safe output and contextual escaping contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: html escaping.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Strings are sequences of bytes with encoding rules, not automatically user-perceived characters. Searching, transforming, matching, and displaying text require attention to Unicode and the output context. In this lesson, focus on html escaping; then compare it with attribute escaping. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use safe output and contextual escaping when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Strings are sequences of bytes with encoding rules, not automatically user-perceived characters. Searching, transforming, matching, and displaying text require attention to Unicode and the output context. For safe output and contextual escaping, begin with html escaping. Also distinguish attribute escaping; url encoding versus html escaping; javascript and css output contexts. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
